$comment: paratext's capability matrix against the three packages it replaces (compat-oracle's LAYERS). Rendered by <CapabilityMatrix pkg="paratext" /> from apps/docs-chassis and held by scripts/capabilities-lock.test.ts: every `ours` yes/partial names a test file and a title substring it contains, or a compat-oracle grade; every incumbent cell names a source at the version compat-oracle grades, and a local source is checked for the text it `quote`s or `lacks`. term-img is not installed in this repository, so its cells cite term-img 7.1.0, the graded version, by URL or through its vendored suite. `n/a` means the row does not apply to that package, and says why. A row that could not be proved for every column is not here.

rows.capability: A hyperlink on a pipe is its text and its URL
rows.why: Where OSC 8 is not understood, a link is written as `Docs (https://x.dev)`, so a log, an agent or a redirected file reads the address instead of escape bytes.

ours.title: projects to `text (url)` on a pipe, and carries no escape at all

ansi-escapes.note: writes the OSC 8 bytes on every stream; it never checks

terminal-link.note: the text, a space and the URL

rows.capability: Every OSC capability has a text form
rows.why: An image becomes its caption, a notification a printed line and a link its text and URL whenever support is absent or unknown, so no OSC byte reaches a pipe.

ours.title: prints something a human can read instead of bytes a pipe cannot

ansi-escapes.note: every OSC helper returns its bytes, whatever the stream

terminal-link.missing: a text form for links only; it has no other capability

term-img.missing: an unsupported terminal throws UnsupportedTerminalError unless the caller passes a fallback function

rows.capability: Hyperlink support detected as supports-hyperlinks detects it
rows.why: `paratext/terminal-link` links on exactly the terminals supports-hyperlinks 4.5.0 says understand OSC 8, and asks about stderr when the link is bound for stderr.
`paratext/term-img` draws on iTerm2, WezTerm, Konsole, Rio and VS Code at the versions term-img names, read from the environment alone.

ours.title: the terminal table is term-img`s, read from the environment alone

ansi-escapes.note: encodes the image for any terminal it is given

rows.capability: A registry of capabilities, extensible by plain objects
rows.why: A capability the package never heard of — a Kitty image, a WezTerm user variable — is registered as an object with an encoding and a fallback, survives a round trip through JSON, and emits through the same call as the built-ins.

ours.title: adds one the package never heard of, written as an object

rows.capability: A capability without a text form is refused
rows.why: A capability with no static projection is refused at registration, with the family's code and a fix, so nothing registered can put raw bytes into a pipe.

ours.title: refuses a capability with no static projection — the one rule 6 has no opt-out for

ansi-escapes.note: no helper has a text form to require

terminal-link.missing: its one link has a text form, and a caller can switch it off

term-img.note: the fallback is optional, and the default is to throw

rows.capability: A checker for capability plugins before they ship
rows.why: `npx paratext check ./kitty.mjs` validates a plugin against the family schema without running its author's code, and exits 1 with a code and a fix when it is refused.

ours.title: refuses a malformed plugin with a code and a fix

ansi-escapes.note: takes no plugins, so has nothing to check

terminal-link.note: takes no plugins, so has nothing to check

term-img.note: takes no plugins, so has nothing to check

rows.why: The escape sequences, the hyperlink detection, the image table and the registry install as one package that depends on nothing.

ours.title: depends on nothing: it is the floor

rows.why: paratext's root is graded by ansi-escapes 7.3.0's own tests, unedited, and its CSI half is byte-exact with it.

ansi-escapes.note: its own suite, the control run

rows.why: `paratext/terminal-link` is graded by terminal-link 5.0.0's own tests, unedited.

terminal-link.note: its own suite, the control run

rows.why: `paratext/term-img` is graded by term-img 7.1.0's own tests, unedited, and passes every case that hands it image bytes.

ours.missing: 6 of 18 cases pass a file path, and paratext/term-img takes image bytes so that node:fs stays out of paratext (D-030)

term-img.note: its own suite, the control run
